A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MedSynapse-V work. The main text, supplementary Sections 5–12, equations, figures and tables are available and readable, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, training dynamics, efficiency measurements and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Table 1 and supplementary robustness and failure analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.4 retain the same meta-query memory synthesis, causal counterfactual refinement and intrinsic memory transition procedures. The architectures, objectives and encoder-free inference procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: The PubMedVision, OmniMedVQA, SLAKE and PathVQA training coverage is unchanged, as are the seven main evaluation benchmarks and supplementary OmniMedVQA modality evaluation. Newly cited tasks in Section 12 are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The reported comparator sets are unchanged. MedMO-8B retains its name, size and scores, although its citation changes from the MedMoE paper in v1 to the MedMO paper in v3. This reference correction does not establish a different evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported splits, sample counts, metrics, model sizes, training budgets, preprocessing, prompts and decoding settings remain unchanged in Sections 3.1, 5, 7 and 10 and Table 3.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component and probe-count ablations, memory-design comparisons, mask-quality robustness tests, training and latent-space analyses, and successful and failed diagnostic cases. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 and Section 5 retain reporting of means over five independent runs. There is no change to repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 retains averages of 61.4% with the anatomical encoder and 59.6% with IMT, while Table 4 retains the IMT modality average of 63.7%.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, memory definitions, reward equations and distillation objectives, including Equations 1–8, are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same novelty, diagnostic accuracy, generalization and inference-efficiency claims. The broader literature survey does not revise these core claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of memory grounding, causal refinement and efficiency remain unchanged. Section 9.2 retains the same limitations involving rare modalities, multiple lesions and subtle features; the future-work discussion is also retained.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including module dimensions, hyperparameters, four A100 GPUs, approximately 38 hours of training, preprocessing and evaluation templates. No new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 12 substantially broadens positioning to memory-augmented reasoning, general VLM reinforcement learning, medical understanding and efficient deployment. The bibliography expands from 69 to 160 works, with 95 additions and four removals. Detailed discussion of MMedPO and output-versus-latent alignment is removed, and the MedMO citation is corrected.

P1.justification: The rewrite is concentrated in Section 12, which changes from two focused discussions to three broader thematic discussions. The overall section order and wording of the method, experiments, supplementary analyses and conclusions remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–16 and Tables 1–10 retain their content and organization. Citation changes cause small text-flow adjustments, including around Table 4, while the expanded related-work section and bibliography reflow the end matter.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the MedMO citation and broadens literature coverage, but Section 12 replaces concrete comparisons with prior medical-alignment methods with long lists spanning topics such as finance and GUI agents, with little explanation of their relationship to MedSynapse-V. This weakens the focus and specificity of research positioning. The decline is limited because the method, empirical evidence and reproducibility information are unchanged.
